dossier_meta.catalog_title: Informal Conjecture (Equality in Theorem 1.1 near the zero-rate threshold)
dossier_meta.statement_text: We suspect that there may even be equality in Theorem 1.1 when $s$ is sufficiently close to $(1 - 1/q)r$, i.e., $R(q+1; r, s) = A_q(r, s) + 1$, though our methods fall somewhat short of proving this.
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 1.1 (from prior work [7]) establishes the lower bound $R(q+1; r, s) \geq A_q(r, s) + 1$ for all positive integers $q, r, s$ with $r > s$. The current paper proves Theorem 1.2, an upper bound showing $R(q+1; r, s) \leq (1+\epsilon)A_q(r, s - cj)$ when $s$ is close to $(1-1/q)r$, but the gap between lower and upper bounds remains. The authors conjecture the lower bound is essentially sharp in this intermediate regime.
